messages:
marta: quick q — where should runtime policy checks live for Private deployments: local agent enforcement or control plane? we need route-level geo restrictions + customer telemetry opt-out.

josh: local agent for enforcement is my preference. avoids extra hop and works offline. but we need signed policy manifests so agents can validate. :thinking:

anika: control plane has the audit trail and centralized policy lifecycle. local enforcement means we either replicate audit locally or accept an audit gap. also secret handling concerns.

sam: propose hybrid: CP defines policies and signs them, agent caches and enforces with short TTLs. control plane pushes updates when available; agent rejects expired/unsigned policies.

marta: what about telemetry opt-out? many Private customers want telemetry kept local — control plane can't just collect raw traces.

josh: agree — opt-out should be a local-only flag. control plane may only receive hashed/aggregated signals if customer allows.

deploy-bot: deploy notice: policy-service v2 rolled to canary in dedicated clusters (tags: policy-cache, signed-manifests). See https://ci/release/2345 :rocket:

josh: example config idea: 

```yaml
policies:
  - id: geo-block
    source: controlplane
    enforcement: agent
    signed_by: cp-key-v2
    ttl: 10m
    audit_sink: local|optional-forwarding
```

anika: revocation is the tricky bit. if CP flags a policy revoked, how does agent learn immediately? need push channel or CRL. short TTL helps but pushes are better.

sam: push via websocket / event stream from CP -> agent. fallback: agent checks signature timestamp and refuses enforcement if last_signed_at > ttl. add a revocation list endpoint agents poll every minute as extra safety.

marta: minimal runtime interface I'm thinking: agent exposes `/policy/apply` (accept signed manifest) and `/policy/events` (sse/ws) to receive revocations. enforcement engine has counters and exposes metrics.

josh: metrics to add: `policy.enforced_count`, `policy.enforcement_failures`, `policy.expired_count`, `policy.signature_failures` and `policy.revoked_applied` (should be zero).

anika: for audits we should log locally to customer-controlled storage and optionally forward an HMACed summary to CP for aggregated visibility. also document KMS expectations for signing keys.

marta: ok action items: 1) I'll draft a short RFC for a hybrid enforcement model (CP-signed policies + agent enforcement + push revocation + local audit sink). 2) include config snippet + minimal agent API. 3) list security constraints (KMS signing, key rotation, signed-timestamp semantics). 4) include telemetry opt-out flow and allowed aggregated signals.

sam: sounds good. one extra: include a failure mode section — agent offline, expired policies, and how fallback to deny/allow should work (deny-by-default recommended).

marta: agreed. I'll file RFC and ping @arch-team for review. please add any links or sample code to the RFC PR. :thumbsup:

josh: +1 

anika: +1, add a paragraph on audit evidence export for compliance customers.

sam: +1 on deny-by-default.

marta: thanks team — I'll post RFC link here once created. :eyes:
